goal: Freeze one deterministic CPU-synthetic scheduler for directed two-GPU P2P and two-agent coherent UMA semantics.
scope: two private-VRAM compute domains and directed single-hop P2P
two compute agents sharing one coherent UMA domain
exact CDC, finite queues, CREDIT and REQUEST_ACK
per-domain pressure, fail-atomic whole-expert placement and live pins
verified Phase5 CompiledAction and ExpertKey/content identity
exact request, token and layer identity across each token routing chain
explicit rejection of frozen missing request, token and layer sentinels
object-granular serialized coherent visibility and checked versions
distinct ACK_OR_CREDIT terminal transition at frozen priority 40
non_goals: measured hardware timing, bandwidth or coherence
adaptive placement, multi-hop, collectives or cache-line protocol
Mixtral, runtime, model or benchmark execution
calibration, DSE ranking or production-scale validation

dependencies.phase3: exact clocks, bridge, EventKey, U128 and SHA-256 primitives
dependencies.phase4: integer service and atomic reservation semantics only
dependencies.phase5: frozen routing, residency and authority identities

assumptions: All operation and placement decisions are compiled before execution.
Synthetic payload bytes and service rates are hash-bound assumptions.
Whole-object functional coherence is sufficient for the Phase 6 minimum.
unknowns: measured P2P, NVLink and UMA service curves
production trace scale and adaptive placement value
alternative_designs: Multiple per-GPU Phase 4 schedulers were rejected because they create multiple time authorities.
Aggregate VRAM pooling was rejected because it hides local capacity failure.
Cache-line coherence was deferred in favor of object-granular functional visibility.
risks: Synthetic rates cannot support hardware latency or bandwidth claims.
Pinned MOVE is rejected rather than delayed in the minimal implementation.
Only two-domain direct paths are validated; multi-hop and collectives remain future work.
validation_method: native Phase 6 and inherited Phase 3/4/5 ASAN/UBSAN execution
directed topology, duplex, credit, capacity and exact routing-chain tests
CDC rational edge and synthetic alignment tests
UMA alias, immutable, version and visibility tests
live object and wire checkpoint tests
R1 blocker regressions for fail-atomic rejection, alignment ranges, frozen priorities, topology IDs, action proofs, expert identity, UMA serialization/invariants and route-key ties
MODEL-P6-R2-B1 negative regressions for missing token identity, route/expert layer mismatch and operation-to-route token mismatch
TRACE-P6-R3-B1 negative regressions for empty request and UINT64_MAX/UINT32_MAX token/layer sentinels
authority, tamper, trailing-byte and topology-mismatch negative tests
sealed run and candidate exact-set validation
acceptance_criteria: three roles GO on one candidate ledger with empty blockers
owner_decisions: Phase 5 GO authorizes Phase 6 CPU-synthetic multi-domain implementation.
Push is permitted after each completed phase.
next_legal_action: After same-hash GO, freeze Phase 6 and implement Phase 7 adapter, collector and profiling application framework locally; any model/GPU execution requires a separate owner-approved server application.
forbidden_actions: modification or reinterpretation of frozen G3 or S4 evidence
